title: C# Questions & Answers - Use of Ref and Out Parameters
sourceFile: Ref & Out Parameters - C# Multiple Choice Questions - Sanfoundry.html
description: This set of C# Multiple Choice Questions & Answers (MCQs) focuses on "Use of Ref and Out Parameters".

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Variable 'i' is passed as a ref parameter (5 + 5 = 10). Variable 'j' is passed as an out parameter (initialized to 6 inside the method, then 6 * 6 = 36).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the ref keyword in C# is true?

options.text: The ref keyword causes arguments to be passed by reference
Any changes made to the parameter in the method will be reflected in the variable when control is passed back
Ref usage eliminates overhead of copying large data items

questions.explanation: The 'ref' keyword indicates that a parameter is passed by reference, allowing the method to modify the original variable.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: The first call is call-by-value (n remains 1 in Main). The second call is call-by-reference (n is updated to 21 in Main).

questions.question: Which parameter passing style does the following C# code use?
questions.explanation: The code demonstrates swapping values using reference parameters, which is a 'Call by reference' mechanism.

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Because of 'ref', the method 'fun' points the 'arr' variable in Main to a new array of size 6. Unassigned positions in a new int array default to 0.

questions.explanation: The code calculates the factorial of 7 (7! = 5040).

questions.question: What will be the output of the following C# code?
questions.explanation: Compilation error occurs because the call uses 'ref b' but the method definition declares 'int p' without the 'ref' keyword.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to pass an argument by reference when the variable must already be assigned?
questions.explanation: The 'ref' keyword is used to pass a variable by reference.

questions.question: Select the parameter list that matches this method call.

options.text: ref int a, int b, ref float c
ref int a, ref float c, ref int b
ref int a, ref int b, float c
ref int a, ref int b, ref float c

questions.explanation: The parameter list in the definition must match the call, using 'ref' for all three arguments.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about ref and out is correct?

options.text: An argument passed to a ref parameter need not be initialized first
Variables passed as out arguments need to be initialized prior to being passed
To use a ref parameter, only the calling method must explicitly use the ref keyword

questions.explanation: Statement (a) is wrong because ref must be initialized. (b) is wrong because out does not need initialization. (c) is wrong because both call and definition must use the keyword. Thus, 'None' is correct.
